page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n2 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions, and AES cryptography. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the n2-highmem-2 delivers average single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1827.69. However, multi-core and memory-intensive operations show significant performance constraints. The multi-core CPU performance is categorized as poor, scoring 1875.88 in stress-ng and 1321.0 in Geekbench. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 102.44 GB/sec for cached small blocks and dropping to 13.86 GB/sec for uncached large block reads. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show weak performance, with gzip compression at 23.53 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 7.99 GB/sec. Specialized workloads like software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing also fall into the bottom tier of benchmarked systems.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel processing or high memory bandwidth. Due to its low multi-core and database operation scores, it is less suited for heavy database engines or high-throughput web serving. Instead, it is best utilized for lightweight caching layers, small-scale memory-intensive applications, basic text processing, or development environments requiring more RAM than standard general-purpose instances without the cost of additional CPU cores.
